Took my first gig in a while recently was pretty run of the mill type thing, go to a planet and do some surveys no hostile encounters in previous many expeditions. The trip there took a while this time few hundred light-years from the station near me where I took the contract the same place I boarded the freighter class that took us there, those suckers got some heavy weaponry all sides of 'em. Big ol' things those freighters big enough to swallow up a few dropships and carry a couple hundred crew depending on the ship itself of course. Variations from ship to ship are pretty common due to the different factions and groups out there, finding different technologies and developing other ideas and theories allowing for new and vast variations throughout the galaxy.

This ship was impressive at first sight approaching its rear you see its enormous engines black with carbon residue rimmed white with a thin layer of ash. Forming a diamond of three on either side in a chevron formation they loom over the docking bay. Sleek sides follow forward covered in blackened heat plates gates and airlocks peppering the sides as well as gun placements in a measured and tedious way. Big crew means a few cooks come along and this time we seemed a bit over staffed but I wasn't complaining. We boarded at a amidships gate with a couple few of the crewmen and wound our way within the maze of corridors weaving through the ship to our bunks to unload some gear and get to work in the kitchens with prep work, inventory and all that stuff gotta be ready I brought some rations for when we head out on the planet just in case each set of 30 crewmen which was a single party in a lander were accompanied by a 3 medics and 2 cooks as well as a few sophisticated androids that were the size of a small vehicle almost dwarfing my little jump ship, suckers are pretty neat.

They drop at the same time as our dropship does and we do a kinda dance on the way down. Filled to the brim with supplies and extra stuff we may need they hit the ground on airbags and tumble something fierce. We usually meet up with em as they right themselves and pop onto their I guess you'd call em legs, they got six three on either side. Got a bit of an attitude to em to like a happy little puppy but the puppy is twice your height and about three of your height long. Thick hatches adorn its every surface pitted with storage ports surrounding its powercell core and inner workings a little screen which is removable and allows for commands to be input. Neat tech those guys.

Carryin' on though landing went fine, trip there was a bit boring but y'keep busy as you can with some of the stuff we get on board. Video and archive access helps a ton to pass the time we got some games too and then you can always head on up to the observation deck and check out the skies. Big ol dome of transparent metal gives a pretty amazing view.

Getting around for a while we stumbled across something though and boy was it somethin to see. Coming over a ridge of red brown stone we had a circular settlement come into view and at its center a crater housing a huge black sphere. The wind etched and scribed monoliths that once were are marked only by the presence of a few stragglers outside the crater. Cousins dot the horizon of the landscape but the town, city even huge in its own right barren and empty not a soul around the whole place.

We made our way down and made camp at the edge as the sun made its way beneath the horizon staining the sky bright orange. Static filled the air and a strange sense of wonder at the buildings that lie before us dawned on all of us. After the dinner rush and cleanup we all just sat in awe and wonder the android faithfully alongside us prone in the dusty sand.

All in all was a pretty boring trip but honestly it's almost better than my vacation was still pretty sore but it's almost completely healed and I should suck it up anyways. The new leg hasn't even needed a tune up that Baynani did a bang up job with it so long as I keep on following her advice it should keep goin fine for years to come.

We packed up and headed home after about a week's stay on this planet about 200 hours or so, a good stint in the field and boy am I glad to be home with some brews, my little home and shop and a comfortable place to rest my soul.

Keep yourselves safe, and eat well kids.
